title: KoreLumina — Master OS - KoreLumina Reconstruction Update

messages.content:
Continue the audit before changing code. We now evaluate Workspace Appearance as a user-facing preference feature layered over the Core Lumina appearance engine, not as backend infrastructure itself.
Run the next range:
Bashsed -n '1001,1500p' \
/tmp/workspace-appearance-production-audit.txt
This range should complete:


LuminaAppearanceProvider


storage behavior


resolver contract


CSS variable application


control wiring


After that, I’ll classify each item as:


Production complete


Transitional Builder scaffold


Core Lumina integration gap


Actual defect


No edits until the audit establishes the remaining functional gaps.

Proceed with the next section of the audit:
Bashsed -n '1501,2000p' \
/tmp/workspace-appearance-production-audit.txt
Then continue with:
Bashsed -n '2001,2500p' \
/tmp/workspace-appearance-production-audit.txt
Do not make changes yet. The goal is to complete the audit and produce a production readiness matrix covering:
AreaStatusNotesArchitectureAppearance stateResolverCSS variable pipelineSurface renderingWorkspace controlsPersistencePreview synchronizationRuntime integrationAccessibilityPerformanceTesting
Once the audit is complete, we'll have a definitive list of:


Fully production-ready components.


Transitional Builder-only pieces that should remain until Core Lumina wiring is finished.


Genuine defects that need fixing.


Missing production features (such as profiles, import/export, per-project appearance, and backend persistence).


At that point we can execute the remaining work in a controlled order rather than continuing with ad hoc fixes.

(base) erictouko@MacBook-Pro korelumina % git status
On branch feature/lumina-workspace-migration
Your branch is up to date with 'origin/feature/lumina-workspace-migration'.

Changes not staged for commit:
  (use "git add <file>..." to update what will be committed)
  (use "git restore <file>..." to discard changes in working directory)
	modified:   apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/appearance/css/applyAppearance.ts
	modified:   apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/appearance/css/variables.ts
	modified:   apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/appearance/resolver/resolveAppearance.ts
	modified:   apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/appearance/resolver/types.ts
	modified:   apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/background/LuminaGlassLayer.tsx
	modified:   apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/surface/LuminaSurface.tsx

no changes added to commit (use "git add" and/or "git commit -a")
(base) erictouko@MacBook-Pro korelumina % 
  [Restored Jul 12, 2026 at 6:02:57 AM]
Last login: Sun Jul 12 06:02:57 on ttys001
Restored session: Sun Jul 12 06:02:11 EDT 2026
(base) erictouko@MacBook-Pro korelumina %

This is a good point to stop and assess before proceeding.
Those six modified files all belong to the same architectural change:


appearance/resolver/types.ts


appearance/resolver/resolveAppearance.ts


appearance/css/variables.ts


appearance/css/applyAppearance.ts


background/LuminaGlassLayer.tsx


surface/LuminaSurface.tsx


They represent one cohesive feature: promoting material rendering (saturation, contrast, brightness, layer opacity) to first-class appearance tokens.
The builds have passed repeatedly, so the changes are at least type-safe and build-clean. However, they have not yet been functionally validated. Based on the audit, there are still open questions:


Are the new CSS variables actually consumed everywhere?


Does LuminaSurface now use the new material tokens consistently?


Does switching between Glass, Solid, and Mica produce the intended visual differences?


Do Preview, Designer, and Developer workspaces all render identically?


I would not commit yet.
Instead, treat this as a pending feature branch. The next step should be functional validation:


Launch the builder.


Open Workspace Appearance.


Exercise every appearance control:


Material (Glass/Solid/Mica)


Tint


Transparency


Blur


Elevation


Glow


Contrast




Verify the visual changes propagate immediately.


Compare Designer, Developer, AI, and Preview workspaces for consistency.


If those checks pass, then commit this as a single logical change, for example:
Bashgit add \
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/appearance/css/applyAppearance.ts \
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/appearance/css/variables.ts \
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/appearance/resolver/resolveAppearance.ts \
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/appearance/resolver/types.ts \
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/background/LuminaGlassLayer.tsx \
apps/lumina-builder/src/components/lumina/surface/LuminaSurface.tsx

git commit -m "feat(appearance): promote material rendering to resolved appearance tokens"
After that commit, continue the broader workspace appearance audit from a clean working tree. That keeps the history aligned with your reconstruction workflow: one architectural feature per commit, followed by the next audit-driven improvement.
